messages:
support-ops: Putting a customer issue here — streaming responses from the TS/Node SDK on an edge runtime are dropping chunks mid-stream when an auth rotation happens. Customer says this started after upgrading their proxy and now sees missing payloads and duplicate billing for aborted streams.
customer-jen: Repro steps I gave them:

1) Using our ts-edge SDK (v0.12.1) on a Vercel edge function
2) Open a streaming generation with token that rotates server-side after ~30s
3) After rotation, stream stops producing chunks; stream appears closed for client but server keeps generating.

I attached logs and a tiny repro. Headers show `Content-Encoding: gzip` and chunked transfer.

Logs excerpt:
```
[edge-proxy] request id=abc123 -> upstream
[upstream] 200 OK, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Encoding: gzip
[edge-proxy] auth-refresh -> 401 to auth server, rotating token
[edge-proxy] proxy: flushed conn -> client; remaining upstream stream aborted
```

support-ops: Thanks Jen. Any chance you can paste the minimal repro code? Also which SDK exact package are you using: `@redwood/inference` or `@redwood/edge-sdk`?
devx-jordan: quick question — is the app running on Vercel Edge? Does the proxy do TLS-termination+gzip? Similar reports we've seen had proxies rewrapping gzip which plays poorly with streaming.
customer-jen: Using `@redwood/edge-sdk` 0.12.1, yes Vercel Edge with a custom reverse proxy in front (nginx on a layer). Minimal client in the edge function:
```
export default async (req) => {
  const resp = await client.stream.create({ model: 'gpt-lite', input: 'long text...' })
  const reader = resp.body.getReader()
  let acc = ''
  while(true){
    const { done, value } = await reader.read()
    if(done) break
    acc += new TextDecoder().decode(value)
    // sometimes we see a big gap here then done
  }
  return new Response(acc)
}
```

eng-runtime-oncall: Noted. Two hypotheses: (1) SDK retry logic on 401 triggers a new upstream request while proxy is mid-gzip-stream, proxy tears connection and returns a short/empty chunk to client. (2) The gzip layer + proxy buffer causes partial flush and the client sees truncated chunk boundaries. Both consistent with a token-rotation event.

Can you share the raw HTTP headers captured at the proxy boundary? Especially `Connection`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Encoding`, and any `Content-Length`/`Content-Range` bits. Also the auth rotation timing.

customer-jen: Headers (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: upstream.internal
Authorization: Bearer ey...old
Accept-Encoding: gzip
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Encoding: gzip
X-Request-Id: abc123
```
Auth server log shows token refresh at 2024-11-07T10:12:25Z, streaming started at 10:11:58Z.

sre-ana: Customer is being billed for the aborted attempts? That's a problem — need to escalate if there are duplicate generation charges. Please capture the `request_id` for each attempt and open a billing review if duplicates exist.

eng-runtime-oncall: Quick triage notes: SDK v0.12.1 had a known edge-case where the retry layer would re-issue a request on 401/403 without preserving streaming handshake headers; this can lead to proxy midstream resets when token rotation happens. We fixed header-preserving retries and backpressure handling in 0.13.0 (PR #4521). Asking devx to confirm if upgrade is viable as a fast mitigation.
devx-jordan: Confirmed — 0.13.0 specifically guards against re-issuing a streaming request mid-flight and keeps `Connection: keep-alive` + `TE: trailers` semantics stable. It also avoids re-wrapping gzipped responses. If you can, try pinning auth for the duration of the stream (no rotation) as a workaround, or upgrade to 0.13.0.

customer-jen: Can you point me to a quick patch? We can't disable rotation long term for security reasons. Our immediate ask is a safe workaround.

eng-runtime-oncall: Workarounds we recommend now: 
- Short-term: pin a single short-lived token for the stream request and refresh only between requests (not during).
- Mid-term: upgrade to 0.13.0 which includes streaming retry fixes.
- Ops: if you must rotate mid-stream, ensure your proxy preserves TCP connection and does not rebuffer/gzip-rewrap (pass-through gzip headers).

Snippet to pin token server-side (Node):
```
// create a ephemeral token for stream
const ephemeral = await auth.createEphemeral({ ttl: 60 })
const resp = await client.stream.create({ auth: ephemeral.token, ... })
```

support-ops: I'll propose the upgrade + billing review. Jen, can you try the ephemeral token test and paste results? If the stream stays stable it's a quick way to confirm cause.

customer-jen: Tried ephemeral token (ttl=60) and re-ran. Streaming completed end-to-end, no chunk drops. Looks promising.

eng-runtime-oncall: Great repro. We'll schedule a fast patch backport to 0.12.x if needed, but recommend upgrading to 0.13.0. I'll open ENG ticket and assign to eng-runtime for follow-up and a backport if customer needs it. PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (header-preserving-retries).

support-ops: Filing billing ticket now and flagging for enterprise support. SRE, please hold until we confirm no duplicate charge.
sre-ana: billing ticket created: B-7920. I'll correlate request ids and refund if duplicates found.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime/patch-4521 -> staging at 2388881105 by eng-runtime-oncall :rocket:

devx-jordan: Follow-ups: add test coverage for gzipped streaming via proxy in our edge CI, and document ephemeral token pattern in troubleshooting guide.

customer-jen: Thanks all, ephemeral token workaround and upgrade plan looks good. Please circle back with the ENG ticket and ETA for backport.

support-ops: Noted. Closing loop once ENG updates ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
